subject: Help with paramaterization of longitudinal model in INLA

messages.author: 32bf4f27a31a68db
messages.subject: Help with paramaterization of longitudinal model in INLA
parts:
Hello,

I'm attempting to build a model with some fixed and random effects.  However, the outcome variable is repeated for each subject, over time.  Plotting the subject's scores clearly indicates a different slope and intercept for each subject.

Doing this in lme4 is simple, but doesn't have an autoregressive term.

m <- lmer(score ~ f1 + f2 + (1+attempts|subject))



Looking through the literature and online examples, I've seen a few different ways of building this.  However, I'm not sure which is the "correct" way.


fm1 <- formula(score ~ f1 + f2 + f(subject, model="iid") + f(subject, attempts, model="ar1")

fm2 <- formula(score ~ f1 + f2 + f(subject, model="iid") + f(attempts, replicate=subject, model="ar1")

# From Faraway book
nid <- length(unique(subject))
subject2 <- subject + max(subject)
fm2 <- formula(score ~ f1 + f2 + f(subject, model="iid2d", n=2*nid) + f(subject2, attempts, copy="subject")


Some questions:
1) fm1 has two labels in the second f().  I don't know how INLA handles this, but is this a correct way to calculate a per-subject slope?
2) fm2 also seems to generate on random effect slope, for each subject, but is this better/different than fm1
3) fm3 comes directly from Faraway book.  However, I can't figure out how to make the per-subject slope have an autoregressive term.

Any thoughts or explanation would be greatly appreciated!!!!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Help with paramaterization of longitudinal model in INLA
parts:
Hi and thx for your email.

I'm not 100% sure about your model...

if you have subjects 1,2,3..., with covariates 'attempts' and you want
to coefficient for 'attempts' to have an AR1 structure, then its like

y ~ ... f(subject, model="iid") +
f(time.subject, attempts, model="ar1", replicate = subject)

where 'time.subject' is the time-point within each subject. There are
some details here, that the the time-points are regular and complete,
otherwise you can give them through the arguments 'values'

y ~ ... f(subject, model="iid") +
f(time.subject, attempts, model="ar1", replicate = subject,
values = 1:10)

which will give you the time-points 1:10 and then 'time.subject' can
be one of them as it like.

the second argument 'attempts' is the covariate which scales the AR1
term. if that argument is missing, its defaults to 1.

I would use the pc.cor1 prior for the correlation in the AR1, as the
simpler model is that its constant, see the Stat.sci paper about
penalized complexity priors from last year.

let me know if you still have issues,

H

Thanks Håvard , that's very helpful!

The "attempt" variable is simply a sequential integer.

Your answer leads me to two quick questions:

1) I'm not entirely clear on the protocol of the f() function.  Are these two equivalent?  If not, how do they differ?
f(subject, model="iid") + f(subject, attempts, model="ar1")
f(subject, model="iid") + f(attempts, replicate=subject, model="ar1")

2) You suggest using the pc.cor1 prior for the AR1 correlation:
      - How do I do this?  Any examples online?
      - How do I estimate good hyper-parameter values for the prior?



Thank you very much!!!!!
